newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Currencies erode Asia debt.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Currencies erode Asia debt.

text.p: Asia started the week with a multi-billion dollar bang but ended it with more of a whimper with currency jitters helping to undercut the market.
"Debt is dead," an Australian banker said in Hong Kong. "Do you want to lend to Korea at the moment?"
Despite the massive country rescue package for Thailand which brings central bankers from across the region, including China, bankers said there was little incentive to lend.
Announced on Monday, the package is tied to an overhaul of Thailand's financial and regulatory infrastructure.
Bankers want to see the outcome of recent rating reviews, repricing of some borrowers, or shorter maturities for other regular issuer debt issuers.
They said the market was also deserted for the August summer break and what deals were done were not big or interesting.
"It's as interesting as a wet weekend in Labuan," a Hong Kong banker said, commenting on the lack of fresh mandates.
In other news, spillover from the Thai crisis hit the Hong Kong market where overnight rates pushed higher and spreads between Hong Kong and U.S. government widened.
In the three-month maturity they swelled by 48 basis points, and 33 basis points in the two-year in the early afternoon, and some Hong Kong debt paper was sold.
"We saw some unloading on Hong Kong dollar floating-rate paper," said a trader at European Investment Bank.
The trader said A2-rated HongkongBank's three-year floating rate certificate of deposit issue widened to more than 30 basis points from 27 basis points at its launch two weeks ago.
Bankers said the long weekend -- Monday is a Hong Kong public holiday -- added to nervousness as traders tried to work out a weekend position.
However, few believe that hedge funds will target the Hong Kong dollar peg, and take on the territory's central bank, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, bankers said.

"George Soros is not a hero," said the head of capital markets at one bank. "He is very rational... You're talking about beating a (central) bank with US$80 billion, (in foreign exchange reserves) and over US$100 billion held by the People's Bank of China.'
Some Indonesian 10-year paper moved out by up to 20 basis points from about 400 basis points over U.S. treasuries overnight Thursday even before the Asian selling started.
In one of the few new deals, Shanghai Wai Gaoqiao Free Trade is borrowing US$50 million through a three-year floating-rate note through arranger Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The issue is at par to float at 120 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
The FRN includes a maintenance of ownership clause from Shanghai Pudong New Area Administration.
Continuing the trend for subcontinental debt issues, a Pakistan telecom may issue a US$250 million seven-year 144a later this month.
The Republic of Pakistan may also issue U.S. dollars backed by remittances from Pakistani overseas workers.
